en: In close approximation; almost, virtually.
With close relation; intimately.

nearly.ety: From near + -ly. Cognate with Scots nerelie, neirlie (“nearly”). Compare also English nearling, nearlings.

ex.en: I was nearly run over by a car.
ex.ja: 危なく車にひかれるところだった。

ex.en: Texas is nearly twice as large as Japan.
ex.ja: テキサスは日本のほぼ二倍ある。

ex.en: Because just one minute costs nearly four pounds.
ex.ja: １分だってほぼ４ポンドかかるんだから。

note.ja: near（近い）+ -ly。「近く」→「ほとんど」。

en: Specific; discrete; concrete.
Specialised; characteristic of a specific person or thing.
A small individual part of something larger; a detail, a point.
A particular case; an individual thing as opposed to a whole class. (Opposed to generals, universals.)

particular.ety: From Middle English particuler, from Anglo-Norman particuler, Middle French particuler, particulier, from Late Latin particularis (“partial; separate, individual”), from Latin particula (“(small) part”). Equivalent to particle + -ar. Compare particle.

ex.en: Do you have anything to say in particular?
ex.ja: 何か特に言う事がありますか。

ex.en: I have no particular reason to do so.
ex.ja: 私にはそうする特別な理由は何も無い。

ex.en: That rule holds good in this particular case.
ex.ja: その規則はこの場合には適用される。

note.ja: part（部分）+ icul（小さな）+ ar。小さな部分の →「特定の・特別な・細かい」。

en: Prior; occurring before something else, either in time or order.
Premature; acting or occurring too soon.
An existing criminal record (short for "previous convictions")
A track record of similar behaviour, especially bad behaviour.

ex.en: I had lost a camera the previous day.
ex.ja: 私はその前日にカメラをなくしてしまった。

ex.en: Tom has two children from a previous marriage.
ex.ja: トムには連れ子が二人いるんだ。

ex.en: I'm sorry, but I have a previous appointment.
ex.ja: 残念ですが、私には先約があります。

note.ja: pre（前に）+ vi（道）+ ous。ラテン語 praevius（先に行く）から。→「前の・以前の」。

en: Rapidly; with speed; fast; with expedition.
Very soon.

quickly.ety: From Middle English quykly, quikliche, quicliche, cwikliche, cwickliche, from Old English cwiculīċe. By surface analysis, quick + -ly.

ex.en: Time goes by quickly when you're having fun.
ex.ja: 楽しんでいるときは時の経つのがはやい。

ex.en: I'll finish it as quickly as I can.
ex.ja: できるだけ早く片付けます。

ex.en: The good news spread through the village quickly.
ex.ja: その吉報は大変すばやく村中に広がった。

note.ja: quick（速い）+ -ly。quick はもと「生きている」の意味（the quick and the dead）。

en: Any considerable and connected part of a space or surface; specifically, a tract of land or sea of considerable but indefinite extent; a …
Such a division of the city of Rome and of the territory about Rome, of which the number varied at different times; a district, quarter, …

region.ety: From Middle English regioun, from Anglo-Norman regiun, from Latin regiō, from regō. Doublet of regio.

ex.en: In the southern region, sales were up 47 percent.
ex.ja: 南部の売り上げは４７パーセント増加した。

ex.en: This video is not available in your region.
ex.ja: この動画はお住まいの地域ではご利用いただけません。

ex.en: The region is a production center for tea leaves.
ex.ja: その地方はお茶の産地です。

note.ja: ラテン語 regio（境界線・地域）から。reg（まっすぐ・支配する）+ ion。支配の及ぶ範囲 →「地域・地方」。

en: A cutting; a part cut out from the rest of something.
A part, piece, subdivision of anything.
To cut, divide or separate into pieces.
To reduce to the degree of thinness required for study with the microscope.

section.ety: From Middle English seccioun, from Old French section, from Latin sectiō (“cutting, cutting off, excision, amputation of diseased parts of the body, etc.”), from sectus, past participle of secāre (“to cut”). More at saw.

ex.en: She is attached to the general affairs section.
ex.ja: 彼女は庶務課に所属している。

ex.en: Do you have a non-smoking section?
ex.ja: 禁煙席はありますか。

ex.en: I asked for a seat in the smoking section.
ex.ja: 喫煙席を頼んでおいたのですが。

note.ja: sect（切る）+ ion。切り分けた部分 →「区分・部分」。insect（体が切れ目で分かれた生き物→昆虫）も同じ sect。

en: A general type.
A person evaluated in a certain way.
To separate items into different categories according to certain criteria that determine their sorts.
To arrange into some sequence, usually numerically, alphabetically or chronologically.

sort.ety: From Middle English sort, soort, sorte (cognate Dutch soort, German Sorte, Danish sort, Swedish sort), borrowed from Old French sorte (“class, kind”), from Latin sortem, accusative form of sors (“lot, fate, share, rank, category”).

ex.en: What sort of fruit do you like best?
ex.ja: どんな種類の果物が一番好きですか。

ex.en: I don't care for that sort of thing.
ex.ja: そのようなことは好きではありません。

ex.en: What sort of television programs are on today?
ex.ja: 今日はどんなテレビ番組がありますか。

note.ja: ラテン語 sors（くじ・運命・種類）から。→「種類・分類する（sort out ＝ 整理する）」。

en: The state of moving quickly or the capacity for rapid motion.
The rate of motion or action, specifically the magnitude of the velocity; the rate distance is traversed in a given time.
Called by the soundman when the recording equipment has reached running speed and is ready to go.
To go fast.
To exceed the speed limit.

speed.ety:
From Middle English sped (“prosperity, good luck, quickness, success”), from Old English spēd (“success”), from Proto-West Germanic *spōdi (“prosperity, success”), from Proto-West Germanic *spōan, from Proto-Germanic *spōaną (“to prosper, succeed, be happy”), from Proto-Indo-European *speh₁- (“to prosper, turn out well”).
Cognate with Scots spede, speid (“success, quickness, speed”), Dutch spoed (“haste; speed”), German Low German Spood (“haste; speed; eagerness; success”), German Sput (“progress, acceleration, haste”). Related also to Old English spōwan (“to be successful, succeed”), Albanian

ex.en: This is the car with the most speed.
ex.ja: この車はスピードが一番はやい車です。

ex.en: In towns, speed is limited to 50 km/h.
ex.ja: 町では速度は50キロに制限されています。

ex.en: He went round the corner at top speed.
ex.ja: 彼はその角をフルスピードで曲がった。

note.ja: 古英語 spēd（成功・繁栄）から。うまく進む →「速さ・速度・急ぐ」。

en: To be on a journey, often for pleasure or business and with luggage; to go from one place to another.
To pass from one place to another; to move or transmit.
The act of traveling; passage from place to place.
A series of journeys.

travel.ety:
PIE word
 *tréyes
From Middle English travelen (“to make a laborious journey, travel”) from Middle Scots travailen (“to toil, work, travel”), alteration of Middle English travaillen (“to toil, work”), from Old French travailler (“to trouble, suffer, be worn out”). See the doublets travail and travois.
Compare typologically routine << Latin rupta via. Note the inverse semantic vectors: travel moves from a subjective state (toil) to an objective action (journey), while routine moves from an objective object (beaten path) to a subjective pattern (habit).
Largely displaced native fare, from Old En

ex.en: In those days, few people could travel abroad.
ex.ja: その当時海外旅行に行ける人はほとんどいなかった。

ex.en: Do you travel by sea or by air?
ex.ja: あなたは船で旅行をしますか、飛行機でしますか。

ex.en: My brother is big enough to travel alone.
ex.ja: 私の兄はもう大きいので十分一人で旅行できる。

note.ja: travail（骨折り）と同語源。昔の旅は苦労の多いものだった →「旅行する・移動する」。

en: The act of touching physically; being in close association.
The establishment of communication (with).
To touch; to come into physical contact with.
To establish communication with (something or someone).

contact.ety: From Latin contactus, from contingō (“to touch on all sides”), from tangō (“to touch”). Used in English since the 17th century.

ex.en: At last, we made contact with the police.
ex.ja: やっと警察と連絡がとれた。

ex.en: I made my first contact with him there.
ex.ja: そこで私は初めて彼と知り合った。

ex.en: I understand you wish to contact your husband.
ex.ja: ご主人と交信なさりたいんですね。

note.ja: con（共に）+ tact（触れる）。互いに触れ合う →「接触・連絡」。intact（触れられていない→無傷の）も同じ tact。

en: A small quantity of liquid, just large enough to hold its own rounded shape through surface tension, especially one that falls from a sou…
A dose of liquid medicine in the form of a drop (sense 1).
Of a liquid: to fall in drops or droplets.
To fall (straight down) under the influence of gravity, like a drop of liquid.

drop.ety:
From Late Middle English droppe, Middle English drope (“small quantity of liquid; small or least amount of something; pendant jewel; dripping of a liquid; a shower; nasal flow, catarrh; speck, spot; blemish; disease causing spots on the skin”) [and other forms], from Old English dropa (“a drop”), from Proto-West Germanic *dropō (“drop (of liquid)”), from Proto-Germanic *drupô (“drop (of liquid)”),, from *dreupaną (“to drip, droop”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰrebʰ- (“to drip, drop”).
Cognates
Cognate with Saterland Frisian Droupe, Druppe (“drop”), Dutch drop, drup (“droplet”), German Tropfen

ex.en: My old friend dropped in at my house.
ex.ja: 旧友が私の家を訪ねてくれた。

ex.en: Be sure to drop in at my house.
ex.ja: 必ず私の家に立ち寄りなさい。

ex.en: Why don't we drop over to see her?
ex.ja: ちょっと彼女のところに寄ってみようじゃないか。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「しずく・ぽとりと落ちる」。しずく、落とす、下がる、やめる（drop the subject）、降ろす（drop off）。

en: Unblemished (figuratively or literally); clean and pure; innocent.
Light in color, pale, particularly with regard to skin tone but also referring to blond and red hair.
Something which is fair (in various senses of the adjective).
A fair woman; a sweetheart.
To smoothen or even a surface (especially a connection or junction on a surface).
To bring into perfect alignment (especially about rivet holes when connecting structural members).
Clearly, openly, frankly, civilly, honestly, favorably, auspiciously, agreeably.
Almost; to a great extent but not literally.

ex.ja: その訴訟の判事は公平ではなかった。

ex.en: A teacher must be fair with his students.
ex.ja: 先生は生徒に公平でなければならない。

ex.en: They fought a fair battle with the enemy.
ex.ja: 彼らは敵軍と正々堂々と戦った。

note.ja: 「公平な・晴れた・色白の」は古英語 fæger（美しい）から、「見本市・市」はラテン語 feria（祝日）から来た別語。

en: A biological structure found in many animals that is used for locomotion and that is frequently a separate organ at the terminal part of …
Specifically, a human foot, which is found below the ankle and is used for standing and walking.
To use the foot to kick (usually a ball).
To pay (a bill).

foot.ety:

ex.ja: なぜ全力をつくさないの？

ex.en: Will you go on foot or by bus?
ex.ja: 歩いて行きますか？それともバスで行きますか？

ex.en: I didn't mean to step on your foot.
ex.ja: 足を踏むつもりはなかったのです。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「足（くるぶしから下）」。足、ふもと（the foot of the mountain）、フィート（足の長さ）。ラテン語 pes、ギリシャ語 pous と同じ祖先 *ped-。

en: A connection between places, people, events, things, or ideas.
One element of a chain or other connected series.
To connect (two or more things).
To demonstrate a correlation between (two things).

ex.en: Please feel free to link to my page.
ex.ja: このページはリンクフリーです。

ex.en: The link that you sent me didn't work.
ex.ja: 君が送ってくれたリンク、開かなかったよ。

ex.en: I removed the English and Japanese language links.
ex.ja: 英語と日本語のリンクを外しました。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「鎖の輪」。輪 →「つながり・連結（する）・リンク」。

en: Included, present, characterized by affirmation.
Formally laid down.
A thing capable of being affirmed; something real or actual.
A favourable point or characteristic.

ex.en: Try to have a positive attitude about everything.
ex.ja: 何事にも積極的な態度を取るようにしなさい。

ex.en: He gave a positive answer to my question.
ex.ja: 彼は私の質問に肯定的な答えをしてくれた。

ex.en: I try to be positive all the time.
ex.ja: 常に前向きでいようと心掛けているんだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 positivus（置かれた・定められた）から。pos（置く）。はっきり置かれた →「確信した・肯定的な・前向きな・陽性の」。

en: In every part of; all through.
In every part; everywhere.
During an entire period of time, the whole time.

throughout.ety: From Old English þurh ūt, equivalent to through + out. Compare German durchaus (“all the way, fully, absolutely”).

ex.en: He has helped the poor throughout his life.
ex.ja: 彼は生涯に渡って貧しい人々を助けた。

ex.en: This country has an even temperature throughout the year.
ex.ja: この国は年間を通して気温の変化がない。

ex.en: It's open ten to six daily throughout the year.
ex.ja: １０時から６時まで年中無休でやっています。

note.ja: through（〜を通って）+ out（すっかり）。「すみずみまで」。

en: A journey through a particular building, estate, country, etc.
A guided visit to a particular place, or virtual place.
To make a journey.
To make a circuit of a place.

tour.ety: From Old French tour, tourn, from the verb torner, tourner.

ex.en: They had plenty of money for the tour.
ex.ja: 彼らは旅行用のお金はたくさんもっていた。

ex.en: I'd like to join a night bus tour.
ex.ja: 夜のバスツアーに参加したいのですが。

ex.en: Where do I book a bus tour?
ex.ja: バスツアーはどこで申し込みするのですか。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 tornos（ろくろ・回転）から。turn（回る）と同じ。ぐるりと回る →「旅行・見学・巡業」。

en: Whose arrival is a cause of joy; received with gladness; admitted willingly to the house, entertainment, or company.
Producing gladness.
Greeting given upon someone's arrival.
The act of greeting someone’s arrival, especially by saying "Welcome!"; reception.
The utterance of such a greeting.
To affirm or greet the arrival of someone, especially by saying "Welcome!".
To accept something willingly or gladly.

ex.en: You are welcome to do anything you like.
ex.ja: 君は勝手に好きな事をしてよろしい。

ex.en: On behalf of the company, I welcome you.
ex.ja: 一同を代表して、歓迎の意を表します。

ex.en: A welcome party took place in the restaurant.
ex.ja: レストランで歓迎パーティーが行われた。

note.ja: well（よく）+ come（来る）。よく来た →「ようこそ・歓迎する・歓迎される」。

en: In an absolute or unconditional manner; utterly, positively, wholly.
Independently; viewed without relation to other things or factors.
Yes, certainly; expression indicating strong agreement.

absolutely.ety:
From late Middle English absolutly, equivalent to absolute + -ly.
First attested in 1425.

ex.en: What's that thing? I have absolutely no idea.
ex.ja: さあ、一体何のことやら。私にはさっぱりわかりません。

ex.en: What did we learn from this? Absolutely nothing.
ex.ja: その教訓は？何もありません。

ex.en: I have absolutely nothing to do with that.
ex.ja: それはまったく関係ないです。

note.ja: absolute（完全な）+ -ly。ラテン語 absolvere（解き放つ）。「制約から解き放たれた」→「完全に・絶対に」。

en: Supplemental or added to something.
Something added.

additional.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin additionalis. By surface analysis, addition + -al.

ex.en: This was an additional fund for buying books.
ex.ja: これは本を買うための足しになった。

ex.en: How much was the additional charge?
ex.ja: 割り増し料金はいくらでしたか。

ex.en: Non-members pay an additional 50 dollars.
ex.ja: 非会員は50ドル増しとなります。

note.ja: addition（追加）+ -al。ラテン語 addere ＝ ad + dare（与える）。「追加の」。

en: Further away than.
On the far side of.
Farther along or away.
In addition; more.
The unknown.
The hereafter.

beyond.ety:
Etymology tree
Old English beġeondan
Middle English biyonde
English beyond
From Middle English biyonde, from Old English beġeondan, from be- + ġeond; related to yonder.

ex.en: The beauty of the sight is beyond description.
ex.ja: その美観は筆では書き表せない。

ex.en: The beauty of that country is beyond description.
ex.ja: その国の美しさは言葉に表現できないほどである。

ex.en: The beauty of the scene was beyond description.
ex.ja: その光景は描写できないほど美しかった。

note.ja: be + yond（向こうに）。→「〜の向こうに・〜を越えて・〜の及ばない」。

en: A state or quality.
A particular state of being.
To subject to the process of acclimation.
To subject to different conditions, especially as an exercise.

condition.ety: From Middle English condicioun, from Old French condicion (French condition), from Latin condicio. An unetymological change in spelling due to a confusion with conditio. Displaced native Old English hād (“state, condition”).

ex.en: The condition of the patients changes every day.
ex.ja: 患者の状況は日ごとに変化する。

ex.en: You must on no condition open the box.
ex.ja: どんなことがあってもその箱を開けてはいけない。

ex.en: The house is not in very good condition.
ex.ja: その家はあまりいい状態ではない。

note.ja: ラテン語 condicio（取り決め）＝ con（共に）+ dic（言う）。一緒に言い交わしたこと →「条件・状態・体調」。

en: Beyond what is due, usual, expected, or necessary; extraneous; additional; supernumerary.
To an extraordinary degree.
Something additional, such as an item above and beyond the ordinary school curriculum, or added to the usual charge on a bill.
An extra edition of a newspaper, which is printed outside of the normal printing cycle, for example to report an important late-breaking …

ex.ja: 深夜勤務手当は出てるの？

ex.en: Could you use an extra pair of hands?
ex.ja: お手伝いしましょうか？

note.ja: ラテン語 extra（外に）から。範囲の外の →「余分の・追加の・エキストラ」。

en: In an immediate manner; instantly or without delay.
Without any intervening time or space.
As soon as, the moment that.

immediately.ety: From Middle English immediatly, equivalent to immediate + -ly.

ex.en: She promised to look into the matter immediately.
ex.ja: その問題をすぐ調べると彼女は約束した。

ex.en: In this activity one immediately sees the result.
ex.ja: この仕事では結果がすぐ分かる。

ex.en: I hope you will correct the situation immediately.
ex.ja: 状況をただちに正していただけるようお願いします。

note.ja: immediate（即時の）+ -ly。in（否定）+ medius（中間）。「間に何も入らない」→「すぐに」。medium と同じ。

ex.en: Nature provides them with the means of survival.
ex.ja: 自然がそうした生き延びるための手段を与えているのである。

note.ja: nat（生まれる）+ ure。生まれつきのもの →「性質・自然」。

en: Moving with speed, rapidity or swiftness, or capable of doing so; rapid; fast.
Occurring in a short time; happening or done rapidly.
Quickly, in a quick manner.
Answer quickly.
Raw or sensitive flesh, especially that underneath finger and toe nails.
Plants used in making a quickset hedge.
To amalgamate surfaces prior to gilding or silvering by dipping them into a solution of mercury in nitric acid.

From Middle English quik, quic (“living, alive, active”), from Old English cwic (“alive”), from Proto-West Germanic *kwiku (“alive, lively quick”), from Proto-Germanic *kwikwaz (“alive, lively, quick”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʷih₃wós (“alive”), from *gʷeyh₃- (“to live”), *gʷeyh₃w- (“to live”). For semantic development, compare lively.
Cognate with Dutch kwik, kwiek (“lively, quick”), German

ex.en: Be quick, or you will miss the train.
ex.ja: 急がなければ汽車に遅れますよ。

ex.en: Get over here and be quick about it!
ex.ja: こっちへ来い、ぐずぐずしないで。

ex.en: I want quick action subsequent to the decision.
ex.ja: 決定の後すみやかに実行に移して欲しい。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「生き生きと動く」。もとは「生きている」（the quick and the dead）。→「速い・すばやい・機敏な」。

en: To transfer goods or provide services in exchange for money.
To be sold.
An act of selling; sale.
The promotion of an idea for acceptance.

sell.ety:
From Middle English sellen, from Old English sellan (“give; give up for money”), from Proto-West Germanic *salljan, from Proto-Germanic *saljaną, from Proto-Indo-European *selh₁-.
Cognates
Cognate with Scots sell (“to sell”), Danish sælge (“to sell”), Norwegian Bokmål selge (“to sell”), Norwegian Nynorsk selja, selje (“to sell”), Swedish sälja (“to sell”), Faroese and Icelandic selja (“to sell”), Gothic 𐍃𐌰𐌻𐌾𐌰𐌽 (saljan, “to pay tribute, make an offer”).

ex.en: I should sell it while it still runs.
ex.ja: まだ動くうちに売ってしまわなきゃ。

ex.en: Tom suggested that Ann should sell the house.
ex.ja: トムはアンが家を売るように提案した。

ex.en: The products are sold on a world scale.
ex.ja: その製品は世界的な規模で販売されている。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「渡して代金を得る」。売る、売れる、（考えを）売り込む。

en: Signifying something; carrying meaning.
Having a noticeable or major effect.
That which has significance; a sign; a token; a symbol.

significant.ety: From Latin significans, present participle of significare, from signum (“sign”) + ficare (“do, make”), variant of facere.

ex.en: But the benefits are significant at all ages.
ex.ja: しかし、その利点は、あらゆる年齢層で大きな意味を持っているのである。

ex.en: The difference in our ages is not significant.
ex.ja: 私たちの年齢の差は重要ではない。

ex.en: The life in the university is significant.
ex.ja: 大学での生活は有意義である。

note.ja: sign（印）+ i + fic（作る）+ ant。印を作る →「意味を示す」→「重要な・意味のある」。signify（示す）も同じ。

en: Except on a specified condition; if not.
If not; used with counterfactual conditionals.

unless.ety: From Middle English unlesse, earlier on lesse (modern on + less), from (not) on lesse (than) (“(not) on a less compelling condition (than)”). The quality of negation in the word and the lack of stress changed on to un-.

ex.en: Unless you stop fighting, I'll call the police.
ex.ja: けんかをやめないと、警察を呼びますよ。

ex.en: Don't speak unless you have something worth saying.
ex.ja: 言う価値のあることがなければ、しゃべるな。

ex.en: You won't be in time unless you run.
ex.ja: 走らなければ間に合わない。

note.ja: on less than（〜より少ない条件で）から変化した語。「〜しない限り」。

en: To be in harmony about an opinion, statement, or action; to have a consistent idea between two or more people.
To give assent; to accede.

agree.ety: From Middle English agreen, from Old French agreer (“to accept or receive kindly”), from a gré (“favorably”), from Latin ad (“to”) + gratum (“pleasing”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *gʷerH- (“to welcome, greet, praise”).

ex.en: She agreed with him about the holiday plan.
ex.ja: 彼女は、休日の計画について、彼の考えに同意した。

ex.en: We agreed to start early the next morning.
ex.ja: 我々は翌朝早く出発することで一致した。

ex.en: I cannot agree with you on this point.
ex.ja: わたしはこの件に関しては君に同意できない。

note.ja: a（= ad 〜へ）+ gree（喜ばしい：ラテン語 gratus）。古フランス語 a gré（意にかなって・快く）から、「相手の考えを快く受け入れる」→「同意する・意見が合う」。grateful（感謝している）、grace（優雅さ）も同じ grat。

en: A traditional Portuguese unit of liquid volume equal to 1.7–2.1 liters depending on the area of Portugal, used particularly for wine.

canada.ety: From Portuguese canada, from Latin cannatus.

ex.en: On the whole, Canada has a severe climate.
ex.ja: 概して、カナダは厳しい気候である。

ex.en: I'd like to mail this package to Canada.
ex.ja: この小包をカナダへ送りたいのですが。

ex.en: Canada is on the north side of America.
ex.ja: カナダはアメリカの北側にある。

note.ja: 先住民イロコイ族の言葉 kanata（村）から。

en: Free of dirt, filth, or impurities (extraneous matter); not dirty, filthy, or soiled.
Of metal, having relatively few impurities.
A removal of dirt.
The first part of the event clean and jerk in which the weight is brought from the ground to the shoulders.
To remove dirt from a place or object.
To tidy up, make a place neat.
Fully and completely.

clean.ety:

Proto-West Germanic *klainī
Old English clǣne
Middle English clene
English clean
From Middle English clene, from Old English clāne, clǣne (“clean; pure; clear”), from Proto-West Germanic *klainī (“dainty, fine, small; clean”), perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *glēy- (“gleaming”), from Proto-Indo-European *gel- (“to gleam”).
Cognates
Cognate with Alemannic German chlei, chli, chlii, chly, klei (“small”), Bavarian gloa, kla, klaa, kloa, kloan (“small; young; insignificant”), Central Franconian and Low German kleen (“small”), Cimbrian khlòan, khlumma (“small”), Dutch and German kle

ex.en: Mary left her sister to clean the windows.
ex.ja: メアリーは妹に窓をきれいにすることを任せた。

ex.en: The water in this river is very clean.
ex.ja: この川の水はとてもきれいだ。

ex.en: I spent all yesterday afternoon cleaning my room.
ex.ja: 昨日の午後はずっと、私の部屋を掃除するのに費やした。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「汚れがない」。きれいな、清潔な、掃除する、公正な（a clean fight）。

en: A programmable electronic device that performs mathematical calculations and logical operations, especially one that can process, store a…
A person employed to perform computations; one who computes.

computer.ety: From compute + -er. Doublet of cantore, counter, and kontor. The sense referring to people first appears c. 1613 in the works of the poet Richard Brathwait. The sense referring to a machine first appears c. 1897 in the magazine Engineering.

ex.en: Everyone will have his own computer before long.
ex.ja: もうすぐみんなが自分のコンピューターを持つだろう。

ex.en: The words would appear on his computer screen.
ex.ja: それらの単語は彼のコンピューター・スクリーンに現れたのだった。

ex.en: The company has purchased a new computer system.
ex.ja: その会社は新しいコンピューターシステムを購入した。

note.ja: compute（計算する）+ -er。com + putare（考える・数える）。「計算するもの」。dispute、reputation と同じ。

en: The process of constructing.
Anything that has been constructed.

construction.ety:
From Middle English construccioun, construction, from Old French construction, from Latin cōnstructiō, from cōnstruere.
Morphologically construct + -ion.

ex.en: Three large buildings near here are under construction.
ex.ja: この近くで３つの大きなビルが建設中だ。

ex.en: The first phase of construction has been completed.
ex.ja: 建設工事の第一段階は終わった。

ex.en: The new bridge is in process of construction.
ex.ja: 新しい橋の建設が進行中だ。

note.ja: con（共に）+ struct（積む）+ ion。積み重ねて組み立てること →「建設」。structure（構造）、destroy（積んだものを崩す→破壊する）、instruct（中に積む→教える）も同じ。

en: A discrete but connected event, situation, or period within a broader sequence, narrative, or life course.
A bounded narrative unit within a television series, constituting a single installment that is structurally discrete yet interrelated wit…

episode.ety: From French épisode, from New Latin *epīsodium, from Ancient Greek ἐπεισόδιον (epeisódion, “a parenthetic addition, episode”), neuter of ἐπεισόδιος (epeisódios, “following upon the entrance, coming in besides, adventitious”), from ἐπί (epí, “on”) + εἰς (eis, “into”) + ὁδός (hodós, “way”).

ex.en: Are there any other interesting episodes in history?
ex.ja: 他にも何か歴史上の面白いエピソードってありますかね？

ex.en: Seriously though, episode 21 made me almost cry while laughing.
ex.ja: でもほんとに、エピソード21には涙が出るほど笑ったよ。

ex.en: How many episodes of One Piece have you watched?
ex.ja: ワンピース、何話見ましたか？

note.ja: ギリシャ語 epeisodion（合唱の間に入る部分）から。epi（加えて）+ eis（中へ）+ hodos（道）。→「出来事・挿話・（連続ドラマの）1回分」。

ex.en: Every boss has his or her favorite employee.
ex.ja: どの上司にもお気に入りの部下がいるものだ。

ex.en: What's your favorite song in last year's top 100?
ex.ja: 去年の上位100曲の中で、一番好きなのは何ですか？

ex.en: What's your favorite thing about the Christmas season?
ex.ja: クリスマスシーズンで一番好きなところは何ですか。

note.ja: favor（好意）+ ite。好意を受けた →「大好きな・お気に入り・本命」。

en: Money one earns by working or by capitalising on the work of others.
Money coming in to a fund, account, or policy.

income.ety: From Middle English income, perhaps continuing (in altered form) Old English incyme (“an in-coming, entrance”), equivalent to in- + come. Cognate with Saterland Frisian Íenkúumen (“income”), West Frisian ynkommen (“income”), Dutch inkomen, inkomst (“income, earnings, gainings”), German Low German Inkumst (“income”), German Einkommen, Einkunft (“income, earnings, competence”), Danish indkomst (“income”), Swedish inkomst (“income”), Icelandic innkváma (“income”).

ex.en: Your income is three times larger than mine.
ex.ja: 君の収入は私の３倍だ。

ex.en: Our income is small, but we get by.
ex.ja: 我々の収入は少ないが、なんとかやっています。

ex.en: The income from this source is tax-free.
ex.ja: ここからあがる所得は無税である。

note.ja: in（中へ）+ come（来る）。中へ入ってくるもの →「収入」。outcome（外へ出てくるもの→結果）と対で覚えやすい。

en: The state or characteristic of being just or fair.
The ideal of fairness, impartiality, etc., especially with regard to the punishment of wrongdoing.

justice.ety:
From Middle English justice, from Old French justise, justice (Modern French justice), from Latin iūstitia (“righteousness, equity”), from iūstus (“just”), from iūs (“right”), from Proto-Italic *jowos, perhaps literally "sacred formula", a word peculiar to Latin (not general Italic) that originated in the religious cults, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂yew-. Doublet of Justitia.
Partly displaced native Old English rihtwīsnes (Modern English righteousness < rightwiseness).

ex.en: No picture can do justice to the scene.
ex.ja: その景色は絵にも表せない。

ex.en: That picture does not do justice to him.
ex.ja: あの彼の写真は実物より悪く撮れている。

ex.en: We should try to treat everybody with justice.
ex.ja: 私たちはすべての人を公平に扱うようにすべきだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 iustitia（正義）から。jus（法・正義）。→「正義・公正・司法・裁判官」。

en: A person whose job is to manage something, such as a business, a restaurant, or a sports team.
The head coach.

ex.ja: ホテルの支配人と話をしたいのですが。

ex.en: Who is the manager of that baseball team?
ex.ja: その野球チームの監督は誰ですか。

ex.en: The manager said, "Let's begin with this job."
ex.ja: この仕事から始めよう、と支配人がいった。

note.ja: man（手）から。イタリア語 maneggiare（手で馬を扱う）→「扱う・管理する」。manage（管理する）、manual（手の→手引き書）も同じ man。

en: Physical motion between points in space.
A system or mechanism for transmitting motion of a definite character, or for transforming motion, such as the wheelwork of a watch.

ex.en: The civil rights movement leads to a dream.
ex.ja: 公民権運動はある夢に至る。

ex.en: He played a major part in the movement.
ex.ja: 彼はその運動で主要な役割を果たした。

ex.en: There are movements to try to ban TV advertising.
ex.ja: テレビ広告を禁止しようとする動きがある。

note.ja: move（動く）+ ment。→「動き・運動・（社会）運動・楽章」。

en: A photograph.
A photo finish.
To take a photograph of.

Ancient Greek -γρᾰ́φος (-grắphos)der.
English -graph
English photographclip.
English photo
Clipping of photograph.

ex.en: Is there a photo shop in the hotel?
ex.ja: ホテルの中に写真屋はありますか。

ex.en: This photo takes me back to my childhood.
ex.ja: その写真を見ると私は子供時代を思い出す。

ex.en: Let me have a look at those photos.
ex.ja: その写真を見せて下さい。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 phos（光）から。photograph（光で描いたもの）の略 →「写真」。

en: The condition or feeling of being safe; security; certainty.
A safety lock or safety catch: a mechanism on a weapon or dangerous equipment designed to prevent accidental firing or operation.
To secure (a mechanical component, as in aviation) to keep it from becoming detached even under vibration.
to secure a firing pin, as in guns, to keep the gun from firing

safety.ety: Inherited from Middle English savete, from Old French sauveté, from earlier salvetet, from Medieval Latin salvitās, salvitātem, from Latin salvus.

ex.en: I'd like a safety check on my car.
ex.ja: 車検を受けたいのですが。

ex.en: You should put safety before everything else.
ex.ja: 何よりも安全を優先すべきだよ。

ex.en: We must put safety before anything else.
ex.ja: 何よりも安全を優先しなければならない。

note.ja: safe（安全な）+ ty。→「安全・安全性」。

en: The location of an event that attracts attention.
The decorations; furnishings, and backgrounds of a stage, representing the place in which the action of a play is set.
To exhibit as a scene; to make a scene of; to display.
To roleplay.
A notice to actors that their performance has ended.

scene.ety: From Late Middle English scene, from Middle French scene, borrowed from Latin sc(a)ena, from Ancient Greek σκηνή (skēnḗ, “scene, stage”). Doublet of scena and skene.

ex.en: The scene from the hotel was very beautiful.
ex.ja: ホテルからの眺めはとても奇麗だった。

ex.en: I couldn't bear to see such a scene.
ex.ja: そんな場面を見るに忍びなかった。

ex.en: The scene brought her words home to him.
ex.ja: その光景を見て彼女の言葉を彼は思い出した。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 skēnē（天幕・舞台）から。舞台 →「場面・現場・光景・景色」。scenery（風景）。

en: A declaration or remark.
A presentation of opinion or position.
Decisive.
To provide an official document of a proposition, especially in the UK, a Statement of Special Educational Needs.

ex.ja: 大統領はその件について声明を発表した。

ex.en: The President is to make a statement tomorrow.
ex.ja: 大統領は明日、声明を発表する予定である。

ex.en: He made a false statement to the police.
ex.ja: 彼は警察に偽りの申し立てをした。

note.ja: state（述べる）+ ment。述べたもの →「声明・陳述」。state は「立てる・据える」から「はっきり述べる」へ。

en: A star, especially when seen as the centre of any single solar system.
The light and heat which are received from the Sun; sunshine or sunlight.
To expose to the heat and radiation of the sun.
To warm or dry in the sunshine.

ex.en: We watched the sun setting behind the mountains.
ex.ja: 我々は太陽が山の後ろに沈むのを眺めた。

ex.en: You can talk about anything under the sun.
ex.ja: どんな事でも話してください。

ex.en: She was left in the sun too long.
ex.ja: その子はあまりにも長く日光にさらされた。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「太陽」。ラテン語 sol（solar 太陽の）と同じ祖先。Sunday（太陽の日）。

en: The quality or state of being able; capacity to do or of doing something; having the necessary power.
The legal wherewithal to act.

ability.ety: First attested in the 1300s. From Middle English abilite (“suitability, aptitude, ability”), from Old French ableté, from Latin habilitās (“aptness, ability”), from habilis (“apt, fit, skillful, able”); equivalent to able + -ity.

ex.en: You will be paid according to your ability.
ex.ja: 給料は君の能力次第だ。

ex.en: He has the ability to do the work.
ex.ja: 彼にはその仕事をこなす能力がある。

ex.en: You should make the most of your ability.
ex.ja: せいぜい自分の能力を活用しなさい。

note.ja: ラテン語 habilitas（扱いやすさ）から。habere（持つ）の仲間。→「能力・才能」。able（できる）。

en: To give public notice of, especially for the first time; to make known.
To pronounce; to declare by judicial sentence.

ex.en: Tom just announced he'd be moving to Boston.
ex.ja: トムがボストンへ引っ越すことを知らせたところだ。

ex.en: Today is the day college decisions are announced.
ex.ja: 今日は大学の合格発表日だ。

ex.en: He announced my statement to be true.
ex.ja: 私の申し立ては本当だと彼は発表した。

en: A wheeled vehicle, generally pulled by a horse.
A passenger car, either drawn by a locomotive or part of a multiple unit.
To train.
To instruct; to train.
Via the part of a commercial passenger airplane or train reserved for those paying the lower standard fares; via the economy section.

To strike down or lay level with the floor; to knock down.

ex.ja: 家庭用品は三階にあります。

To undergo growth; to be present (somewhere).
An illicit cannabis farm.

ex.en: The sick boy is growing stronger each day.
ex.ja: その病気の子供は日々よくなりつつある。

en: To cause (a person or animal) physical pain and/or injury.
To cause (somebody) emotional pain.
Wounded, physically injured.
Feeling physical or emotional pain.
An emotional or psychological humiliation or bad experience.
A band on a trip hammer's helve, bearing the trunnions.

ex.ja: フットボールの試合でけがをしたのかい？

ex.en: I am sorry if my words hurt you.
ex.ja: 私の言葉であなたが傷ついたならごめんなさい。

note.ja: 古フランス語 hurter（ぶつける）から。→「傷つける・痛む・けが」。過去形も hurt。

en: A visual or other representation of the external form of something in art.
A file on a computer containing a single frame; an image file.
To represent by an image or symbol; to portray.
To reflect, mirror.

image.ety: From Middle English ymage, borrowed from Old French image, from Latin imāgō (“a copy, likeness, image”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eym-; the same PIE root is the source of imitari (“to copy, imitate”); see imitate. Doublet of imago.

ex.en: The company is trying to improve its image.
ex.ja: その会社はイメージアップをはかっている。

ex.en: He is the very image of his father.
ex.ja: 彼は父親に生き写しだ。

ex.en: She is the very image of her mother.
ex.ja: あの子、お母さんそっくりね。

note.ja: ラテン語 imago（像・模倣）から。imitate（まねる）と同じ祖先。→「像・画像・イメージ・印象」。

en: A means of indemnity against a future occurrence of an uncertain event.
The business of providing insurance.

insurance.ety:
From the older form ensurance, see also assurance.
By surface analysis, insure + -ance.

ex.en: Please mail this form to your insurance company.
ex.ja: この用紙を保険会社に郵送してください。

ex.en: He reported the accident to his insurance company.
ex.ja: 彼は、その事故を保険会社に報告した。

ex.en: He took a job with an insurance company.
ex.ja: 彼は保険会社に就職した。

note.ja: in（〜に）+ sure（確かな）+ ance。確かなものにすること →「保険」。ensure（確実にする）、assure（保証する）と同じ。

en: More than half (50%) of some group.
Any share or fraction that is bigger than any one of its counterpart shares or fractions (of the same whole).

majority.ety: From Middle French maiorité, from Medieval Latin maiōritātem, accusative of Latin maiōritās, from Latin maior (“greater”). Morphologically major + -ity.

ex.en: We have a majority interest in the company.
ex.ja: 私達は５０％以上の出資をしている。

ex.en: The president shall be selected by majority vote.
ex.ja: 大統領は投票の過半数をもって選ばれる。

ex.en: He won the election by a large majority.
ex.ja: 彼は選挙で大勝した。

note.ja: ラテン語 maior（より大きい）から。より大きい方 →「大多数・過半数」。minority（少数派）と対。

en: A belief, judgment or perspective that a person has formed, either through objective or subjective reasoning, about a topic, issue, perso…
The judgment or sentiment which the mind forms of persons or things; estimation.

opinion.ety: From English opine + -ion, from Middle English opinion, opinioun, from Anglo-Norman and Middle French opinion, from Latin opīniō, from opīnor (“to opine”). Displaced native Old English wēna.

ex.en: We had a good opinion of your son.
ex.ja: 我々は君の息子さんを立派だとおもっている。

ex.en: Opinions are divided on the issue of taxes.
ex.ja: 課税問題で意見が分かれている。

ex.en: I could not help but state my opinion.
ex.ja: 意見を述べずにはいられなかった。

note.ja: ラテン語 opinari（思う）から。→「意見・見解・評価」。

en: Pertaining to the world as understood through the senses rather than the mind, having to do with the material world.
In accordance with the laws of nature; now specifically, pertaining to physics.
A physical examination.
A physical manifestation of psychic origin, as through ectoplasmic solidification.

physical.ety: Borrowed from Late Latin physicālis, from Latin physica (“study of nature”), from Ancient Greek φυσική (phusikḗ), feminine singular of φυσικός (phusikós, “natural; physical”), from φύσις (phúsis, “origin, birth; nature, quality; form, shape; type, kind”), from φῠ́ω (phŭ́ō, “grow”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰuH- (“to appear, become, rise up”).

ex.en: Physical contact with a child is very important.
ex.ja: 子供とのスキンシップを大切にしないとね。

ex.en: Mental health is as important as physical health.
ex.ja: 精神的な健康は、肉体的な健康と同じくらい大切です。

ex.en: The physical fitness courses are required for everyone.
ex.ja: 体育の授業は全員が必修です。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 physis（自然）から。自然の・物の →「物質の・身体の・物理的な」。physics（物理学）。

en: An advantage of something, especially when contrasted with its disadvantages (cons).
A person who supports a concept or principle.
In favor of.
Professional.

pro.ety: From Late Middle English pro, from Latin prō (“on behalf of”).

ex.en: Pro baseball is interesting these days.
ex.ja: 最近のプロ野球はおもしろい。

ex.en: He has remained pro-conservative throughout.
ex.ja: 彼は保守党一辺倒で押し通した。

ex.en: Let's put together a pro-soccer team for Nagasaki!
ex.ja: 長崎にプロサッカーチームをつくりましょう！

note.ja: professional の短縮。もう一つの「賛成」はラテン語 pro（〜のために）からで、pros and cons（賛否）。

en: To extend, stretch, or thrust out (for example a limb or object held in the hand).
To give to someone by stretching out a limb, especially the hand; to give with the hand; to pass to another person; to hand over.
The act of stretching or extending; extension.
The ability to reach or touch with the person, a limb, or something held or thrown.

reach.ety:
From Middle English rechen, from Old English rǣċan (“to reach”), from Proto-West Germanic *raikijan, from Proto-Germanic *raikijaną, from the Proto-Indo-European *Hreyǵ- (“to bind, reach”).
Cognate with Dutch reiken, German reichen.

ex.en: Go straight ahead until you reach the church.
ex.ja: 教会に着くまでまっすぐ行きなさい。

ex.en: Put the matches out of reach of children.
ex.ja: マッチは子供の手の届かないところに置きなさい。

ex.en: It was dark when I reached the hotel.
ex.ja: ホテルに着いたときは暗くなっていた。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「手を伸ばして届く」。到着する、届く、手を伸ばす、連絡がつく（reach him by phone）。

ex.ja: フランスへの出張がうまくいったことを祈っています。

Quick in physical movement; of an agile and vigorous body; nimble.
A person or thing that is acting or capable of acting.
Any component that is not passive. See Passivity (engineering).

ex.ja: 彼の頭脳の働きは活発だった。

ex.ja: 彼はその革命で積極的な役割をした。

The executive part of government; the persons collectively who are entrusted with the execution of laws and the superintendence of public…

administration.ety: From Middle English administracioun, from Old French administration, from Latin administratio, from administrare; see administer; compare French administration. Equivalent to administrate + -ion.

ex.en: He's in charge of administration at the hospital.
ex.ja: 彼は病院の管理運営に責任がある。

ex.en: We need someone who has some experience in administration.
ex.ja: 経営管理に経験のある方を求めます。

ex.en: The administration cannot but look for alternative sources of revenue.
ex.ja: 政府は他の歳入源を考え出すほかない。

note.ja: ad（〜に）+ minister（仕える）+ ation。仕えて管理すること →「管理・行政・政権」。minister（大臣＝仕える人）。

en: To come or go near, in place or time; to move toward; to advance nearer; to draw nigh.
To play an approach shot.
An act of drawing near in place or time; an advancing or coming near.
An act of coming near in character or value; an approximation.

approach.ety: From Middle English aprochen, borrowed from Old French aprochier (modern French approcher), from Late Latin appropiāre, a verb based on Latin prope (“near”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *pro- (a variant of *per- (“before, in front; first”)) + *-kʷe (“suffix forming distributives from interrogatives”)).

ex.ja: この問題を別の面から取り組んでみよう。

ex.en: With the approach of Christmas, business improved somewhat.
ex.ja: クリスマスが近づくにつれて景気はいくらか回復した。

ex.en: My boss told me I'm hard to approach.
ex.ja: 「君はとっつきにくいね」と社長に言われてしまいました。

note.ja: ap（〜へ）+ proach（近い）。ラテン語 prope（近くに）から。近づく →「接近する・取り組み方」。

en: A disease in which the cells of a tissue undergo uncontrolled (often rapid) proliferation.
Something damaging that spreads throughout something else.

cancer.ety: Borrowed from Latin cancer (“crab”), a calque of Ancient Greek καρκίνος (karkínos, “crab; ulcer; cancer”), possibly cognate, applied to cancerous tumors because of a supposed resemblence between their enlarged veins and the legs of a crab. Doublet of canker and chancre.

ex.en: My uncle died of cancer two years ago.
ex.ja: 私の叔父は２年前ガンで死んだ。

ex.en: I had my only son die of cancer.
ex.ja: 私はガンで一人息子に死なれた。

ex.en: His father had died of cancer 10 years ago.
ex.ja: 彼の父親は１０年前にガンで死んでいた。

note.ja: ラテン語 cancer（カニ）から。腫瘍の周りの血管がカニの足のように広がることから。かに座も Cancer。

en: Having to do with people and government office as opposed to the military or religion.
Behaving in a reasonable or polite manner; avoiding displays of hostility.

civil.ety:
From Middle English cyvyl, civil, borrowed from Old French civil, from Latin cīvīlis (“relating to a citizen”), from cīvis (“citizen”) ultimately from proto-Indo-European *ḱey-. Cognate with Old English hīwen (“household”), hīrǣden (“family”). More at hind; hird.
(polite): Compare typologically urbane (<< Latin urbs), courteous (akin to court).

ex.ja: 公民権運動はある夢に至る。

ex.en: I wonder when the Civil War started.
ex.ja: 南北戦争はいつ始まったのかしら。

ex.en: I will write him a civil answer.
ex.ja: 彼に丁寧な返事を書くつもりです。

note.ja: ラテン語 civis（市民）から。市民の →「市民の・民間の・礼儀正しい」。city（都市）、civilization（文明）も同じ。

en: A sequence of rhythmic steps or movements usually performed to music, for pleasure or as a form of social interaction.
A social gathering where dancing is the main activity.
To move with rhythmic steps or movements, especially in time to music.
To leap or move lightly and rapidly.

en: The action of defending or protecting from attack, danger, or injury.
A strategy and tactics employed to prevent the other team from scoring; contrasted with offense.
To employ defensive tactics (so as to block).

defense.ety: From Middle English defens, defense, from Old French defens, defense, from Late Latin dēfēnsa (“protection”). Displaced native Old English bewering. The verb is from the noun.

ex.en: Tom claims he shot Mary in self-defense.
ex.ja: トムは正当防衛でメアリーを射ったと主張した。

A playing card of that suit.

en: The quality of being organized.

organization.ety: Borrowed from Middle French organisation, from Medieval Latin organizātiō; by surface analysis, organize + -ation.

ex.ja: その団体はどの政党とも関係がありません。

ex.ja: その組織について何か聞いたことはありますか。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 organon（道具・器官）から。器官のように組み立てること →「組織・団体」。organ（器官）。

en: To keep safe; to defend; to guard; to prevent harm coming to.
To book a passenger on a later flight if there is a chance they will not be able to board their earlier reserved flight.

protect.ety: Attested in English since 1530, from Latin prōtēctus (“covered, protected”), past participle of prōtegō, prōtegere (“to cover the front, protect”) from prō, prō- (“before, in front of”) + tegō, tegere (“to cover”), see tegument. ex.ja: 自分を守る方法を子供たちに教えるべきだ。

en: A piece of knowledge that is hidden and intended to be kept hidden.
The key or principle by which something is made clear; the knack.
Being or kept hidden.

The noun is from Middle English secret, from Latin sēcrētum. Doublet of secretum. Displaced Old English dēagolnes (“a secret”).

ex.ja: それは秘密にしておいた方がいい。

ex.en: We found a secret door into the building.
ex.ja: 我々はその建物に入る秘密の扉を発見した。

ex.ja: どんな事情があっても決してその秘密をもらしてはいけない。

note.ja: se（離れて）+ cret（ふるい分ける）。ふるい分けて離しておいたもの →「秘密」。secretary（秘密を任される人→秘書）も同じ。

en: Older.

An old person.
Someone older than someone else (with possessive).

ex.ja: もし今日が日曜日なら、私は釣りにいくのだが。

ex.ja: パーティーは次の日曜日に行われる予定です。

en: Something that happens to someone by chance, a chance occurrence.

en: The state of being married.

en: Required, essential, whether logically inescapable or needed in order to achieve a desired result or avoid some penalty.

necessary.ety:
From Middle English necessarye, from Old French necessaire, from Latin necessārius (“unavoidable, inevitable, required”), variant of necesse (“unavoidable, inevitable”), probably from ne or non cessum, from the perfect passive participle of cēdō (“yield; avoid, withdraw”); see cede.

A person or animal that receives health care from a doctor, nurse, dentist, allied health practitioner, or other person educated in healt…
The noun or noun phrase that is semantically on the receiving end of a verb's action.

en: Something that one uses to achieve an objective, e.g. raw materials or personnel.
A person's capacity to deal with difficulty.
To supply with resources.

ex.en: The boy observed the growth of the plant.
ex.ja: その少年は植物の成長を観察した。

ex.en: Many workers were laid off at that plant.
ex.ja: その工場では多くの労働者が解雇された。

note.ja: ラテン語 planta（若枝・足の裏）から。足で踏み固めて植える →「植える・植物・工場（据え付けられた設備）」。
